**How it works**
- Trims surrounding whitespace, then tries the three accepted shapes with anchored regexes:
  - `<day> <month> <year>` — 1–2 digit day, month as full English name or 3-letter abbreviation in any case, 4-digit year.
  - `DD-MM-YYYY` / `DD/MM/YYYY` — exactly two digits per part, day first.
  - `YYYY-MM-DD` — exactly four/two/two digits.
- Month lookup accepts only an exact full name or an exact 3-letter prefix (`nov`, `NOV`, `November` all work; `Novem`, `Sept`, `Nove` do not).
- Range validation uses a hand-written Gregorian leap rule (`year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0)`) and per-month day counts: bad day or month → `RangeError`; unrecognised shape or unknown month name → plain `Error`. No `Date` parsing is used.
- Output is zero-padded `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**Verified behaviour**
- Accepted: `"5 Nov 2026"`, `"05 November 2026"`, `"5 nOvEmBeR 2026"`, `"29 Feb 2024"`, `"29 Feb 2000"`, `"05-11-2026"`, `"05/11/2026"`, `"2026-11-05"`, plus leading/trailing whitespace variants.
- `RangeError`: `31/04/2026`, `29 Feb 2026`, `29 Feb 1900`, `2026-13-01`, `00/01/2026`, `2026-02-29`, `00/00/2026`, `31 Apr 2026`, `32/01/2026`.
- Plain `Error` (constructor is exactly `Error`): `"Novem"`, `"5 Novem 2026"`, `"5 Sept 2026"`, `"5-11-2026"`, `"2026-1-05"`, `"05-11-2026"`-style mixed separators, double internal spaces, non-strings (`null`, `undefined`, numbers), `""`.

One judgement call: I treat only exact 3-letter abbreviations as valid (so `"Sept"` is an unknown month → plain `Error`), matching the spec's wording rather than real-world usage.
